title: Marvisak/VIctory
body:
An attempt at running GTA VI on PC

README 節錄：# VIctory Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files the user supplies. The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use otherwise. title: sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill
body:
Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization

README 節錄：# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from `PROMPT.md`. ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. title: fxceless/victory-fork
body:
Work-in-progress fork of VIctory: getting an Xbox Series title to render and run on a Windows PC. No game files.

README 節錄：# VIctory fork **As of 27 November 2026 this repository is based on VIctory-NVIDIA by trustno1-coder.** Its tree at commit `959dcaf` replaces this fork's own line of work. **Why.** On the PC this fork was developed on (GeForce RTX 4070, 32 GB of RAM), VIctory-NVIDIA runs the title clearly better. In a 25-minute play session at 2560x1440 it averaged about 17 frames a second in the open world and took about half the frame time of this fork's last code in the busiest scenes, which averaged about 10 frames a second at a lower render size. The two sessions did not cover the same scenes, so these are not a controlled comparison; the gap was large enough to settle the choice. This fork therefore stops its own line and builds on VIctory-NVIDIA from now on. **Credit.** Everything below this section, and the code in this repository, is the work of trustno1-coder and the contributors to VIctory-NVIDIA (see that repository's history and the Credits section further down), built on VIctory by Marvisak and its contributors. title: sybil-solutions/skill-distill
body:
Distill a good Claude Code / Codex session into a skill an open-weight model can follow to reproduce the task

README 節錄：# skill-distill A frontier model did a task well. Can an open-weight model do the same task, given the right instructions? `skill-distill` is a skill for Claude Code or Codex (the **teacher**). You call it at the end of a good session and name a **student**: an agent harness plus a model, for example omp with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The teacher then loops: 1. reads the session and writes a skill for the student; 2. starts the student in tmux, on a fresh copy of the starting state, with the original prompt and the skill; 3. compares what the student produced with what the reference produced; 4. finds the first place the student went wrong and fixes the skill there; 5. runs again, three trials per version, until the student matches the reference. You make the final call: the teacher shows you the reference and the student's best results side by side, and the skill counts as done only when you accept it. The result is two things: the reusable **operator skill** in this repo, and a **produced skill** for one task, one model and one harness. ## Install ``` git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/skill-distill ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.claude/skills/skill-distill # Claude Code ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.agents/skills/skill-distill # Codex ``` Requirements: `tmux`, `git`, Python 3.10+, and the student harness inst

title: ProjectLeonida/mandy
body:
A continuation of Leonida, the Xbox > PC port interface for GTA VI

README 節錄： Leonida Continued Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy. Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord | Telegram Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. > [!NOTE] > **This is a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project.** The original > author has left the project, and development continues here with its full commit history. Credit for the work up to > that point belongs to NotRexed and the contributors listed in the history. Discord: https://discord.gg/ETf4qj5acN Telegram: https://t.me/mandyport ## Project stat

Run locally with Docker for personal use, development, and testing. Go Bot remembers your context and stays attentive to what matters to you, bringing useful discoveries and ideas into the conversation on its own. Teams can use Alibaba Cloud Elastic Container Instance (ECI) to build their own personal agent products, with a dedicated Host for each account, optional persistent storage, and room for their own frontends and service integrations. - **Web research and browser automation.** Search the web through a configured provider. Use Chromium to navigate pages, interact with forms, and capture screenshots. - **Image generation and editing.** Generate images from text or use uploaded images as references. Results appear directly in chat. - **Office documents.** Read, create, and edit Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files with OfficeCLI, and deliver them as downloadable attachments. - **Long-term memory and cross-session recall.** Save user preferences and agent notes per account, and search past conversations when a task needs earlier context. - **Proactive discovery and follow-up.** Enable proactive assistance to let the agent gather and connect relevant information, explore new leads, and share useful findings and suggestions

title: Show HN: bouncemarket – a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
body: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky. Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not. title: lsernau/grh-lean
body:
A short Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis

README 節錄：# GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, in Lean 4 Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The proof is based on Levent Alpöge's, with Claude (https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf). This repository is a shorter version, produced in collaboration with my colleagues at Anthropic, and Claude. ## Two editions - `grh/`: readable edition, about 300,000 lines. Start at `grh/GUIDE.md`. - `grh-compact/`: the same five theorems, about 76,000 lines. Each folder is its own Lake project with its own README. ## Build Needs Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib at commit 56a00585. In either folder: lake exe cache get lake build lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean A build takes one to two hours on 12 cores with 24 GB of memory (about 85 minutes more if the Mathlib cache is missing). ## Status The proof has passed machine checks only, listed in each folder's README. No mathematician has read it through, and no paper comes with it. ## License Apache 2.0, Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC. See `LICENSE`, and `NOTICE` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` in each folder.

title: zortos293/XSEmu
body:
Experimental Xbox Series X|S (GDK) title runner for Windows, built on the XCL translation layer: D3D12.X to D3D12, RDNA2 shaders to DXIL.

README 節錄： # XSEmu **Run Xbox Series X|S (GDK) titles on Windows, built on the XCL translation layer.** XSEmu runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) titles on Windows x64. It is built on XCL, a compatibility layer by ivall and its contributors, and it works the way Wine does: the title's x64 code runs natively on the host CPU, and XCL stands in for the console libraries that Windows does not have. XSEmu does not emulate the console's CPU or hardware. ## Contents - Status - How it works - Shader pipeline - Requirements - Build and test - Usage - Repository layout - Upstream and licence - Legal ## Status XSEmu is experimental research software. Expect crashes, missing features and rendering errors. This repository makes no compatibility claims for any title. The upstream README records the results that XCL reported; those are XCL's results, not XSEmu's. ## How it works `XSEmu run` maps the title's executable and DLLs into its own process and runs them on the host CPU. Each import goes to an XCL replacement, the title's own DLL, the Windows DLL of the same name, or a logged stub. Graphics calls go through a D3D12.X layer that creates real PC D3D12 objects. ```mermaid flowchart TB run["XSEmu run"] --> loader["PE loader loader.rs, pe.rs, tls.rs"] loader -->|maps and starts| title["Title EXE and DLLs native x64 code"] title -->|imports| resolver{"Resolver"}
